A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAEBench study. All 42 pages of each version, including Appendices A–J, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE evaluations, architecture comparisons, scaling experiments, training dynamics, and control experiments in Section 4 and Appendices E–J.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the architecture comparisons and extensive appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The evaluation procedures, including SCR, TPP, feature absorption, RAVEL, and unlearning, remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix D. No algorithmic component, objective, or model architecture is revised.

E1.justification: The training corpora, five sparse-probing datasets, RAVEL tasks, and WMDP-bio/MMLU evaluations are unchanged. RAVEL already appears in v1; correcting the metric count does not add coverage. Vision and biology models are mentioned only as future extensions.

E2.justification: Table 1 lists the same seven SAE architectures in both versions, despite the abstract correcting eight to seven. The PCA, residual-stream, MLP-neuron, and RAVEL skyline comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The training budgets, model configurations, sparsity sweeps, data splits, sample sizes, metrics, and intervention settings in Appendices B and D are unchanged. Adding RAVEL runtime information does not establish a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The random-initialization controls, dictionary-scaling analyses, training-checkpoint evaluations, and intervention-size studies in Appendices E–H are unchanged, including their figures and findings.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises seed counts, repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds RAVEL timings of 45 minutes per SAE and 45 minutes for setup, changing the reported totals from 65 to 110 and 107 to 152 minutes, respectively. This expands runtime accounting; the benchmark performance plots and architectural rankings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The SAE equations and mathematical definitions of loss recovery, absorption, SCR, TPP, and normalized KL divergence are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract corrects the stated scope from seven to eight metrics and from eight to seven architectures, matching content already present in v1. The central claims about proxy-metric limitations, Matryoshka performance, and scaling tradeoffs remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly acknowledges that baselines outperform SAEs on some tasks and explains that sparse probing and absorption serve diagnostic purposes. The conclusion also suggests extensions to vision and biology models. These are limited additions to interpretation and applicability.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code/model repository address, updates the results-browser location, and supplies previously omitted RAVEL runtime information. Implementation details remain unchanged. Release information is still inconsistent because Section 4 retains the promise to release SAEs after peer review.

R1.justification: Appendix D newly uses the already-cited Paulo et al. (2024) finding of agreement between LLM and human judgments to support automated interpretability evaluation. This modestly expands the connection to prior evidence; the cited-work set and main related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and count corrections, adds an Author Contributions section, and updates authorship, affiliations, and acknowledgements. The section organization and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a RAVEL row, while front matter and reference formatting are adjusted, including better wrapping of long URLs. Figures remain unchanged. Figure 12's caption changes seven metrics to eight, although its unchanged plot contains seven metric panels.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency and usability through clearer metric qualifications, explicit resource addresses, more complete runtime accounting, and improved reference formatting. The scientific evidence is unchanged. These gains are limited by stale runtime prose contradicting Table 2 and the newly incorrect eight-metric caption for Figure 12, but support a small net improvement.
